# L1 Regularized Linear Regression
## Purpose 
Linear Regression is a common regression approach.
It fits the best linear relationship between a response variable Y and one or more feature variables X.
This is done by fitting coefficients b such that the model $Y = f(X, b)$ is a reasonable predictor of Y.
The typical approach to do this is by minimizing the mean squared error. 
$ \sum_i (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2 = \sum_i(y_i - (b_0 + b_1 x_i))^2 $
However, the model can overfit if the training error is minimized. 
Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too well. 
This causes poor performance when generalizing to new data. 
Regularization helps prevent overfitting by introducing a penalty for large coefficients.
